instructions: In a large bowl, stir together the flour, yeast, baking powder, sugar and 1/2 tsp of the salt.
Add the yogurt, the milk (lukewarm) and 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil. Stir until it comes together, then knead on a lightly floured counter for 5 minutes, until smooth and a little tacky.
Put the dough back in the bowl, cover with a towel, and leave it somewhere warm for about 1 hour, until doubled. Make the filling while it rises.
Finely chop the onion. Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the pine nuts and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden. Transfer them to a small bowl.
Add the olive oil and onion to the same skillet. Cook over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft. Transfer to a bowl.
Turn the heat up to medium-high. Add the ground beef and 1 tsp of the salt. Break it up with a spoon and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until the liquid has cooked off and the beef starts to brown.
Return the onion to the pan. Add the seven spice, sumac, paprika and black pepper. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the pine nuts.
Taste the filling. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt. Let it cool for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 425°F, with the racks in the upper and lower third. Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Punch down the dough, divide it into 16 pieces and roll each into a ball. Cover and leave for 10 minutes.

Roll each ball into a circle about 4 inches across. Put 1 heaping tbsp of filling in the middle. Fold up the edges to make an open triangle or an open round, pinching the corners to seal them and leaving the filling uncovered in the middle.
Put the pies on the baking sheets and brush the dough with 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the edges are golden. Swap the sheets between the racks halfway through.
Brush the hot pies with the last 1 tbsp vegetable oil. This makes 16 pies. Serve warm or at room temperature with plain yogurt or a green salad.
Packed for lunch, they keep in the fridge for up to 3 days. They also freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat them in a 350°F oven for 7 to 10 minutes, or eat them cold.
method_notes: Cookin' with Mima and Hadia's Lebanese Cuisine both cook a spiced beef or lamb filling, cool it fully, and fill a yeast dough rolled into small rounds, baked at 425 to 430°F. Mima's seasons with seven spice, sumac and paprika and adds pine nuts, while Hadia's uses tomatoes, cinnamon and cayenne and chills the filling overnight. None of the versions had 20 ratings (Mima's has 5 from 9 votes, Hadia's has none, Simply Lebanese has 1), so this is a fallback: it follows Mima's, halved to 16 pies, closed on top as an open pie. Honest time is about 2 hours, mostly the dough rise.
